question: What exactly is a vesicovaginal fistula (VVF)?

options.A: An abnormal opening between the bladder and the vagina
options.B: A blockage in the tube carrying urine from the kidney
options.C: A complete failure of the kidneys to produce urine
options.D: An infection of the lining inside the urinary bladder

explanation: You nailed it! A VVF creates an unwanted channel between these two organs, which is why urine leaks through continuously. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h1)

question: What is the main sign you will notice in a patient with a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Inability to pass any urine at all for several days
options.B: Passing bright red blood clots instead of normal urine
options.C: Severe sharp pain and burning sensation during urination
options.D: Continuous and uncontrollable leakage of urine from the vagina

explanation: Spot on! Because urine bypasses the normal valve completely, it leaks out constantly without the patient being able to hold it. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h1)

question: In Nigeria, what is the leading cause of vesicovaginal fistula?
explanation: Great job! When labour is stuck, the baby's head presses hard against the pelvis, cutting off blood supply and causing tissue to break down. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h2)

question: Which of these patients has the highest risk of developing an obstetric fistula?

options.A: A young rural mother who laboured at home for three days without skilled help
options.B: A middle-aged woman being treated for an uncomplicated bladder infection
options.C: A pregnant woman who attends all her routine antenatal care appointments
options.D: An older woman scheduled for an elective Caesarean section at a tertiary hospital

explanation: Spot on! Days of unmanaged labour without emergency care is the classic pathway to tissue damage and fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h2)

question: Which physical finding is the classic hallmark of a patient with a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: Total absence of urine output for over 48 hours
options.B: Inability to walk due to paralysis of both legs
options.C: Severe lower abdominal swelling and tenderness
options.D: Continuous leakage of urine from the vaginal vault

explanation: You got it! Constant wetness is the tell-tale sign because urine flows straight into the vagina instead of collecting in the bladder. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h3)

question: Why do fistula patients often develop painful sores on their inner thighs?

options.A: Continuous exposure of the skin to the irritating effects of urine
options.B: A rare allergic reaction to hospital bedsheets and blankets
options.C: Fungal skin infections spread from poor personal hygiene
options.D: Pressure sores caused by sitting in a wheelchair for too long

explanation: Exactly! Constant dampness breaks down the skin barrier, leading to painful irritation and excoriation around the thighs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h3)

question: What is a major focus when caring for a fistula patient BEFORE her surgery?

options.A: Applying heavy makeup to distract from the patient's visible sadness
options.B: Discharging the patient immediately after the initial medical diagnosis
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to keep the bladder completely dry
options.D: Improving nutritional status and treating any active infections

explanation: Spot on! Good nutrition helps tissues heal much faster, and clearing infections ensures the body is ready for surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical emotional challenge faced by women with a VVF?

options.A: Severe social isolation from family and community
options.B: Anxiety about whether the surgical repair will succeed
options.C: Deep depression and profound loss of self-esteem
options.D: Feelings of complete invincibility and overconfidence

explanation: Correct! VVF patients deal with heavy emotional stress, stigma, and depression—definitely not overconfidence. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h4)

question: What is the main reason an indwelling catheter is left in place after fistula surgery?

options.A: To deliver strong liquid antibiotics directly into the kidneys
options.B: To flush out remaining blood clots from the abdominal cavity
options.C: To keep the bladder empty and prevent pressure on the repair site
options.D: To measure the patient's exact blood pressure every hour

explanation: You're right! Keeping the bladder deflated allows the newly stitched tissue to heal peacefully without stretching. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h5)

question: You notice a post-op fistula patient has stopped draining urine into her catheter bag. What should you check first?

options.A: The surgical repair has already completely healed within two days
options.B: The patient has started drinking too much water too quickly
options.C: The patient's kidneys have permanently stopped working overnight
options.D: The catheter tubing might be blocked with mucus or a blood clot

explanation: Spot on! A sudden stop in urine flow usually means a blockage in the tube that needs your quick assessment and possible flushing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h5)

question: Why is vocational training an important part of holistic fistula care?

options.A: It teaches the patient how to use specialized machinery to clean hospital linen
options.B: It helps survivors regain financial independence and rebuild their lives after social stigma
options.C: It acts as a substitute for medical treatment when surgery fails to close the hole
options.D: It trains the patient to perform minor surgical repairs on other women in the village

explanation: Great job! Learning a trade empowers these women economically, helping them bounce back from poverty and isolation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)

question: What is the most effective public health strategy for preventing obstetric fistulae in communities?

options.A: Improving access to skilled birth attendants and emergency obstetric care
options.B: Administering daily vitamin supplements during the third trimester
options.C: Providing free diapers to all women living in rural communities
options.D: Encouraging women to give birth at home without professional assistance

explanation: You nailed it! Getting help quickly during difficult labour prevents the prolonged pressure that causes fistulas. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)
